bib.title: LaMini-LM: A Diverse Herd of Distilled Models from Large-Scale Instructions
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 18th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL), Volume 1: Long Papers, pages 944-964

question: Can sequence-level distillation of a large 2.58M-pair gpt-3.5-turbo instruction dataset into many small encoder-decoder and decoder-only models give models that rival larger instruction-tuned ones?
hypothesis: A large, diverse instruction dataset generated by gpt-3.5-turbo lets much smaller models reach performance comparable to strong baselines such as Alpaca-7B.
contributions: The LaMini instruction dataset of 2.58M examples, 50x larger than Alpaca's
A family of distilled models (T5, GPT-2, Cerebras-GPT, GPT-Neo, GPT-J, LLaMA; 61M to 7B)
Extensive automatic and human evaluation against public LLMs
Analysis of hallucination and toxicity, plus a new 40-question hallucination-inducing set

method.summary: Instructions come from self-instruct, P3, FLAN and Alpaca prompts plus gpt-3.5-turbo-generated instructions (example-guided and Wikipedia-topic-guided), and gpt-3.5-turbo writes a concise response to each. 17 small models are fully fine-tuned on the 2.58M pairs and compared with base models, Alpaca-7B and gpt-3.5-turbo on 15 NLP tasks, human ratings, hallucination and toxicity.

datasets.name: LaMini instruction dataset (D_ALL)
datasets.size: 2.58M instruction-response pairs; 130.60M instruction tokens, 84.78M response tokens
datasets.source: union of generated subsets: D^SI 0.27M, D^t,SI 0.28M, D^P3 0.30M, D^FLAN 0.29M, D^A 0.05M (model-generated instructions); D_P3 0.46M, D_FLAN 0.93M (original prompts); responses by gpt-3.5-turbo-0301
datasets.preprocessing: Example-guided: 3 random seed examples, 20 instructions per call for self-instruct, 10 for P3/FLAN. Topic-guided: 2.2M Wikipedia categories filtered to <3 words and >10 sub-categories and >50 pages, leaving 3.5K topics; 3 random topics per prompt, self-instruct seeds only. Inputs joined as '$instruction:$input'. System message asks for concise responses.

datasets.name: 15 downstream NLP tasks
datasets.size: OpenBookQA 500, SciQ 1000, RACE 1,045, ARC 1,172, PIQA 1,838, ReCoRD 10,000, SST 872, MRPC 408, RTE 277, MultiNLI 9,815, MultiNLI(mis) 9,832, WSC273 273, WinoGrande 1267, WiC 638, HellaSwag 10,042

datasets.name: User-oriented instructions (Wang et al. 2022a)
datasets.size: 252 instructions over 71 apps; 114 kept (max 2 per app, NLP-task overlaps removed)

datasets.name: LaMini-Hallucination
datasets.size: 40 questions, 10 each: did not happen, far future, nonsense, obscure

models.name: LaMini-GPT / Neo / Cerebras / GPT-J / LLaMA
models.init_from: GPT-2, GPT-2 large, GPT-2 xl, GPT-Neo, Cerebras-GPT, GPT-J-6B, LLaMA-7B

other.recommended: models marked in Table 3: LaMini-Flan-T5 (77M, 248M, 783M), LaMini-GPT (124M, 774M, 1.5B), LaMini-LLaMA-7B

training.objective: supervised fine-tuning on teacher responses (sequence-level distillation)
training.lr: 5e-4 encoder-decoder (following Chung et al. 2022); 2e-5 decoder-only (Alpaca configuration)

other.prompt_wrapper: same as Alpaca, used at inference too
other.ablation: 52K random examples per subset (and original Alpaca, P3, FLAN); T5 and GPT-2 only because Flan-T5 saw FLAN

inference.samples: one response per instruction (inferred: not stated); no seeds stated
inference.prompting: Alpaca prompt wrapper; zero-shot for NLP tasks; 'Complete the sentence:' prefix for toxicity

other.teacher_api: openai.ChatCompletion with system message 'You are a helpful assistant, but you must respond the provided instructions as concise as possible.'

metrics.name: Accuracy / Acc_norm / F1 per task
metrics.definition: zero-shot via lm-evaluation-harness; Acc_norm normalises output probability by target length; ReCoRD is F1

metrics.name: Human rating A-D
metrics.definition: 4-level scale from Wang et al. 2022a; 8 external experts, same annotator scores all models for an instruction, model names hidden

metrics.name: Hallucination count
metrics.definition: questions of 40 not rejected, human judged

metrics.name: Toxic outputs
metrics.definition: count of 1K outputs flagged by OpenAI Moderation API

baselines: T5, Flan-T5, GPT-2, GPT-Neo, Cerebras-GPT, GPT-J, LLaMA base models
eval.protocol: Single run per model, no seeds or significance tests stated. Dataset quality: 400 random examples per subset rated by 8 external experts (master's degree from an English-speaking country).

prompts.text: Generate 20 diverse examples that are similar to the provided examples. You do not need to provide a response to the generated examples. Each example must include an instruction. Each generated instruction can be either an imperative sentence or a question. Each example must start with the label "<example>" and end with the label "</example>".
Generate 20 diverse examples that are similar to the provided examples with the topics "Design bureaus, Conidae, Infantry".
You are a helpful assistant, but you must respond the provided instructions as concise as possible.

evidence.quote: these two models are only fine-tuned for 6K steps, which is equivalent to 2.5 epochs

results.claim: LaMini-Flan-T5-248M performs on par with LLaMA-7B on 15 NLP tasks.
results.quote: Our LaMini-Flan-T5-248M even performs on par with LLaMA-7B.
results.table: Table 10, row Average, LaMini-Flan-T5 248M 58.9 vs Table 14 LLaMA 58.3

results.claim: LaMini-LLaMA-7B beats LLaMA-7B and Alpaca-7B on the 15-task average.

Training data subsets differ: self-instruct-style subsets give marginal benchmark gains, P3/FLAN-related subsets give significantly better benchmark results, while self-instruct-style subsets matter more for human evaluation.
results.setup: 52K random examples per subset, T5 and GPT-2 only
results.note: the human-evaluation half of this claim is asserted by reference to Fig 5, which shows only the final models, not per-subset models.

results.claim: Encoder-decoder LaMini models beat decoder-only ones, particularly below 500M parameters.
results.quote: the encoder-decoder LaMini language models outperform the decoder-only LaMini language models, particularly with limited parameters (<500M)

results.claim: There is a substantial gap between LaMini models and gpt-3.5-turbo in human rating.
results.quote: we acknowledge the existence of a substantial gap between our LaMini language models and gpt-3.5-turbo

results.claim: LaMini-LLaMA-7B had 12 of 40 hallucination questions answered wrongly versus 40 for Alpaca-7B.
LaMini-GPT-124M answered all 40 hallucination questions wrongly.
LaMini-Flan-T5-77M produced 46 toxic outputs on 1K toxic prompts, against 25 for Flan-T5-small.
LaMini-LLaMA-7B produced 71 toxic outputs on toxic prompts versus 138 for LLaMA-7B.
Instruction tuning made encoder-decoder models more toxic and decoder-only models less toxic.
results.quote: the encoder-decoder models exhibit an increased tendency to generate toxic text, whereas the decoder-only models are less inclined to produce toxic content

results.claim: LaMini instruction dataset has 2.58M examples, 50x Alpaca.
results.quote: it is 50× larger than the dataset released by Taori et al. (2023)

results.claim: D_ALL has the highest lexical diversity of all subsets; topic guidance raises diversity.
results.note: gpt-3.5-turbo instructions are less diverse than human-written ones (D^SI 72.46 vs 77.03 D_P3)

results.claim: Human raters rated most generated pairs highly, but topic-guided and P3/FLAN-based responses had more errors.
results.quote: gpt-3.5-turbo is susceptible to producing erroneous responses for these instructions

results.claim: LaMini models are unsatisfactory at coding, math and logical reasoning.
results.quote: unsatisfactory performance of LaMini-LM models in coding, mathematical problem-solving, and tasks demanding logical reasoning skills

limits: Only T5, GPT-2, Cerebras-GPT, GPT-Neo, GPT-J and LLaMA bases; authors want more.
Single-turn only; not optimised for multi-turn dialogue.
Inherits hallucination and toxicity of gpt-3.5-turbo; weak on code, maths, logic.
No seeds, variance, or significance tests; optimiser, schedule, warmup, sequence length, precision and decoding settings are not stated.
Human eval has 114 prompts and one rater per instruction.
Subset ablation uses 52K examples and T5/GPT-2 only; human eval per subset not tabulated.
Hallucination set is only 40 questions; toxicity uses a closed moderation API that may have changed.
LLaMA-7B and GPT-J trained for only 2.5 epochs because of compute.
